Google invites applications from highly qualified physicists and nuclear engineers for the position of Radiological Subject Matter Expert (SME) in the CBRNE team within the Responsible Development and Innovation (ReDI) team.

The successful applicant will be hired for a Research Scientist position serving as a technical expert evaluating and mitigating safety risks of frontier AI models (primarily but not limited to LLMs) in the radiological domain; specifically, model assistance in radiation and neutron transport modeling, radiation detector defeat and shielding optimization, reactor operations and monitoring, and radiological source managing in a demonstrably unclassified and non-export controlled manner.

Artificial intelligence will be one of humanity’s most transformative inventions. At Google DeepMind, we are a pioneering AI lab with exceptional interdisciplinary teams focused on advancing AI development to solve complex global challenges and accelerate high-quality product innovation for billions of users. We use our technologies for widespread public benefit and scientific discovery, ensuring safety and ethics are always our highest priority.

We are pushing the boundaries across multiple domains. Our global teams offer diverse learning opportunities and varied career pathways for those driven to achieve exceptional results through collective effort.
Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $174000 - $252000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google.

Responsibilities

  • Construct threat models prioritizing vulnerabilities, threat actors, and scenarios related to fission, fusion, thermonuclear weapons development, and high-energy-density dual-use regimes.
  • Create evaluation datasets of complex physics and nuclear engineering prompts to elicit the maximum capability of the model to determine how to uplift malicious actors (e.g., revealing tacit knowledge, novel procedures, time/cost reduction, detectability reduction) across the domain.
  • Collaborate with engineers to design mitigations that block harmful outputs without overly degrading the model's scientific utility. Similar to writing capability evaluations, this requires a deep understanding of dual-use science.
  • Support development and refinement of Google’s nuclear safety policy. Communicate complex risks, evaluation findings, and mitigation strategies to leadership and technical/non-technical external stakeholders.
  • Develop mathematical and computational frameworks to quantify capability thresholds, technical feasibility, and potential consequences of model uplift wherever possible.

Minimum qualifications:

  • PhD and Postdoctoral research experience in Particle Physics, Plasma Physics, Nuclear Engineering, or a related field.
  • 3 years of experience in research with US national laboratories or security initiatives (e.g., IAEA, NNSA, DARPA, or academic consortia).
  • Experience in research or policy in radiological/nuclear security, safeguards, nonproliferation, material control, or threat reduction.
  • Experience in radiation/neutron transport, reactor monitoring, detection, dosimetry, shielding defeat, and RDD/RED mechanics.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience applying ML to radiation detection, detector calibration, or nuclear/particle event reconstruction.
  • Experience in AI safety, evaluations, red-teaming, or applied AI research in lab, academic, or industry settings.
  • Experience in data analysis, scientific computing (e.g., Python or C++), and simulation in neutron/radiation transport, detector response, or plume dispersion.
  • Experience using AI models/agents to enhance capabilities and lower technical barriers.
  • Ability to design evaluations and mitigations that are demonstrably unclassified and non-export controlled by developing dual use science proxies for weapons topics. Highly collaborative, comfortable with peer review, and committed to respectful teamwork.

extra.html:
DeepMind is building frontier financial reasoning and agentic capabilities across Gemini and our enterprise agent harnesses. Moving AI from a generalist research assistant to an agent that can autonomously complete financial workflows requiresmore than raw pre-training scale - it requires deep domain mechanics embedded directly into how models are post-trained, how agent harnesses and tools are architected, and how evaluations measure real-world finance.

As a Finance Subject Matter Experts (SME), you will work with models, evaluations, and post-training data in the following three Finance domains -

  • Quantitative Trading
  • Corporate Finance - specifically with experience across FP&A, Audit and Tax
  • Alternative Asset Management

Unlike traditional advisory roles that stop at high-level feedback or static prompt writing, you will sit directly in the model development loop alongside Research Scientists, Post-Training Engineers, and Product Managers. You will prioritize differentiated financial workflows, design end-to-end financial benchmarks, construct atomic and deterministic grading rubrics, diagnose multi-step agent trajectories, repair near-miss model reasoning traces, design verifiable reward signals, and co-build domain-specific agent skills.

Artificial intelligence will be one of humanity’s most transformative inventions. At Google DeepMind, we are a pioneering AI lab with exceptional interdisciplinary teams focused on advancing AI development to solve complex global challenges and accelerate high-quality product innovation for billions of users. We use our technologies for widespread public benefit and scientific discovery, ensuring safety and ethics are always our highest priority.


We are pushing the boundaries across multiple domains. Our global teams offer diverse learning opportunities and varied career pathways for those driven to achieve exceptional results through collective effort.
Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $207000 - $300000 (USD) + 20% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google.

Responsibilities

  • Evaluate the AI's step-by-step process across calculations, ledger searches, and code to pinpoint quantitative or accounting errors.
  • Create realistic financial tasks (e.g., valuations, backtests, audits) and write "gold-standard" examples to correct model near-misses.
  • Build complex prompts featuring vague instructions, GAAP/non-GAAP differences, and conflicting estimates to test AI resilience.
  • Create pass/fail checklists for deliverables and draft deceptive, polished-but-wrong answers to stress-test automated graders.
  • Teach the AI to efficiently use core financial tools (SQL, etc) and categorize error patterns into reusable templates.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Master's degree in Finance, Economics, quantitative fields, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5 years of institutional finance experience in investigative, modeling-intensive roles (Quantitative Trading, Corporate Finance, or Alternative Asset Management).
  • Experience with frontier LLMs, coding agents, or AI evaluation pipelines, including structured prompts and tool-use traces.
  • Experience identifying flaws in AI-generated financial models, backtests, or memos, and translating these errors into generalizable grading rules.

Preferred qualifications:

  • CFA, CPA, MBA, JD, Master of Financial Engineering (MFE), or an advanced quantitative degree in Finance, Computer Science, Math, or Economics.
  • Background building benchmarks, rubrics, or SFT/RLHF pipelines at AI labs, fintechs, or quantitative teams.
  • Domain-specific excellence in Python and SQL (Quant) or advanced, macro-free spreadsheet software and Python/SQL (Alternative Asset Management/Corporate Finance).
  • Familiarity with market data feeds, SEC EDGAR, Capital IQ, FactSet, Bloomberg, ERP/EPM, and tax/audit platforms.
